To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the combination of LIDAR, semantic and image information, in a context-based system, improves the performance of the pedestrian detection system; and 2) the use of a support vector-based down sampling method allows a reduction of the cardinality of training sets, with a small decrease in performance.
the proposed system, using the SVM-cascade as image-based detector, achieves a true positive rate of 0.92 and a false positive rate of 3.4, when tested on a set of 200 frames of the LIPD dataset.

(i) the proposed system is able to detect pedestrians in complex urban environments, with a high detection rate and low number of false positives; (ii) the proposed context-based approach is able to improve the performance of the system in comparison to the baseline approach, which uses only image-based information; and (iii) the down sampling method is a viable solution to reduce training and testing times of image-based classifiers.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following contributions: (i) the development of a multisensor system for pedestrian detection, (ii), the use of contextual information, obtained from a digital map of roads, to improve the performance of the system, and (iii), a down sampling method, based on multiple linear-SVM, to reduce the cardinalities of training sets and, as a consequence, to decrease CPU-time during the process of image-based training.
